title: The 5 Biggest Cats on Earth, Ranked (The Lion Is Only #2)

scenes.text: The five biggest cats on Earth, by weight. The king of the jungle isn't number one.

scenes.label: Leopard · about 200 lb
scenes.text: Number five: the leopard. A big male reaches about 200 pounds, and still hauls its kill up a tree.

scenes.label: Cougar · 220 lb
scenes.text: Number four: the cougar, or mountain lion. Males reach about 220 pounds, a little more than a leopard.

scenes.label: Jaguar · about 300 lb
scenes.text: Number three: the jaguar, the biggest cat in the Americas. Around 300 pounds, with jaws that can crush a skull.

scenes.label: Lion · 550 lb
scenes.text: Number two: the lion. A big male weighs up to 550 pounds, and the females do most of the hunting.

scenes.label: Siberian tiger · 660 lb
scenes.text: Number one: the tiger. A Siberian male can weigh 660 pounds, and the largest have passed 700.

description:
The five biggest cat species on Earth, ranked by the weight of a large wild male.
Siberian tigers are the largest cats alive: males typically weigh 180 to 306 kg (up to about 660 lb), with exceptional animals over 320 kg. African lion males reach about 250 kg (550 lb). The jaguar, the largest cat in the Americas, reaches roughly 125 to 150 kg depending on the source, the cougar about 100 kg (220 lb) and the leopard about 90 kg (200 lb). Sources differ by a few kilograms, so treat the numbers as rounded. The liger, a lion-tiger hybrid, can be heavier than any of them but exists only in captivity and is not a species.
Which cat did you expect at number one?
first_comment: The cheetah and the snow leopard just miss the list at up to about 160 pounds each. Which cat would you put at #1, and what should we rank next?
